exposure: High transverse skin incision during cesarean delivery
Low transverse (Pfannenstiel) skin incision during cesarean delivery
outcome: Composite wound morbidity (wound infection, fascial dehiscence, incisional hernia, therapeutic wound vacuum, reoperation)
Individual components of the composite outcome
cohort: The study included 328 morbidly obese patients (BMI >=40 kg/m(2)) who underwent cesarean delivery at a single center from 2017-2020.
finding: High transverse skin incision for cesarean delivery was strongly associated with increased composite wound morbidity and wound infection in morbidly obese patients compared to low transverse incision.
mod_finding: High transverse skin incision during cesarean delivery was associated with 3.64-fold increased odds of composite wound morbidity and 5.73-fold increased odds of wound infection in morbidly obese patients.
